# Code review: subscription plan-change endpoints

**Fix one thing before opening the PR.** The new `uuidPipe` changes the error code on four existing billing endpoints, from 400 to 422, for any malformed `spaceId`. It very likely also breaks an existing e2e test that nothing in CI runs. Everything else is small.

Full review: 9 areas checked, 8 of 9 findings adjudicated. No code was changed, no tests were run, nothing was posted.

| | |
|---|---|
| Scope | 23 files, +1748 −43 · base `8be0434` → HEAD `21153d5` (committed work only) |
| Repo | safe-client-gateway · TypeScript/NestJS/Fastify · vitest · biome + tsc · rules from AGENTS.md (10 non-negotiables) + `docs/agents/*` |
| Verdict | **Fix first, then open** |
| Score | **86 / 100** (my estimate; 8 of 9 adjudicated) |
| Held down by | Regression (the 400 → 422 change), then Testing |
| Fix first | REG-001 |
| Adjudication | 8 of 9 · 6 confirmed · 1 contested · 1 refuted · 1 promoted from a deferral |

## Scores by area

| Area | Score | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Regression | 75 | 1 medium |
| Testing | 80 | 3 low, 1 nit |
| Bugs | 90 | 1 low |
| Architecture | 95 | 1 contested, 1 refuted |
| DRY | 97 | 1 nit |
| KISS | 98 | 1 nit, promoted from a deferral, not adjudicated |
| Security | 100 | none |
| Performance | 100 | none |
| Conventions | 100 | none (SPDX headers, pipes, DTO pairing and the elevation table all check out) |

## What this review did not cover

- No tests were run, as you asked. REG-001's "the e2e test is now red" comes from reproducing NestJS's own pipe code in isolation, not from running the suite.
- BUG-001 depends on what the live billing catalog contains, which can't be seen from the repo.
- I didn't write `.git/safe-code-review/last-run.tsv`, since you asked for a review with no file writes, so a re-run won't show a "since your last run" section.

## Fix before opening

**REG-001 · Medium · P2 · 4 existing GET routes answer 422 instead of 400 for a malformed `spaceId`**
`src/modules/billing/routes/billing.controller.ts:95` (also `:134`, `:160`, `:188`; same pairing on the new routes at `:233`, `:279`)
- **What happens:** the second `spaceId` binding used to have no pipe. It now uses `uuidPipe` (`ValidationPipe(UuidSchema)`, whose default code is 422). NestJS resolves param pipes concurrently (`router-execution-context.js:162`, `Promise.all`). The synchronous `ValidationPipe` throw settles one microtask before `SpaceIdPipe`'s `async` rejection, so the 422 always wins.
- **Reproduced:** both adjudicators, and my own script, ran NestJS's real `PipesConsumer` logic:
  - `not-a-uuid` → 422
  - a UUID that `UUID_REGEX` accepts but `z.uuid()` rejects (e.g. `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`) → 422 where it used to be 404
- **Existing test:** `billing.controller.e2e-spec.ts:220` is untouched by this diff and still expects `400`. The e2e project isn't run by `yarn test` or by CI (`ci.yml:163,234` run only the unit and integration projects), so nothing would catch it failing.
- **Fix:** pick one:
  - give the pipe the same status: `new ValidationPipe(UuidSchema, HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST)`;
  - validate the second binding with `UUID_REGEX`, which is what `src/modules/entitlements/routes/guards/space-id-param.schema.ts:6-10` does on purpose;
  - have `SpaceIdPipe` return both the id and the uuid, so the param is bound once.

  Then run `yarn test:e2e` for the billing spec.

## Worth a ticket or a quick follow-up (all P3)

| ID | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| BUG-001 | `billing.service.ts:254` vs `payment-link-offer.rules.ts:71` | The "already on this plan" check compares price ids, but the offer filter drops links by plan **name**. Switching monthly ↔ annual within one plan name would return 403 "plan not available". Both adjudicators confirmed the code path. Whether it happens depends on the live catalog. |
| TST-001 | `billing.controller.ts:62` | No test tells `uuidPipe` apart from `SpaceIdPipe`. That's how REG-001 went unnoticed. Add a malformed-`spaceId` case for the new routes, and a UUID that the regex accepts but zod rejects. |
| TST-002 | `billing.service.ts:196-198` | The preview's same-plan 409 has no test; only the PATCH version is tested. |
| TST-003 | `billing.service.ts:169-206` | The docstring says a preview works for a canceled subscription. No test shows it, so adding a status gate later would stay green. |

## Nits

| ID | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| TST-004 | `billing-api.service.ts:314` | Nothing tests `encodeURIComponent(subscriptionId)`. It changes nothing today, because `opaqueIdPipe` only allows `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. |
| DRY-001 | `billing.service.ts:184-198` / `:232-255` | The not-found and same-plan guards are repeated in both methods. The refuter weakened this: the status check that differs is deliberate and documented. |
| KISS (promoted) | `billing-api.service.ts:260,266` | `updateSubscription` is `async` with `return await this.parse(...)`; its four siblings just `return this.parse(...)`. KISS handed this to architecture, which didn't file it, so I promoted it. Not adjudicated. |

## Contested (no score impact)

- **ARC-001:** `billing.service.ts:205,259`. The new methods call the `IBillingApi` datasource directly, with no repository. The validator confirmed this breaks the rule in `module-structure.md:43`. The refuter pointed out that the module has never had a repository and 6 methods already do this. It's a candidate for a future billing-repository ticket, not something to fix in this PR.

## Ruled out

- **ARC-002:** new code in legacy `src/datasources/billing-api/` is allowed. `module-structure.md:89-93` only bans new sibling client directories, and `IBillingApi` is shared with the entitlements module.
- **Performance, security and conventions came back clean.** The main checks behind that:
  - ownership: `findOwnedSubscription` scopes the lookup to the customer;
  - `paymentLinkId` is checked against the offered links, not trusted;
  - the PATCH has `ElevationGuard` and appears in the gated table;
  - the whole Redis key is cleared on update;
  - the new `patch` method goes through `buildUrl`.

## Worth tidying (optional)

1. Fold REG-001's fix and TST-001 into one change: bind `spaceId` once and add one discriminating test.
2. If you do DRY-001, add TST-002 and TST-003 first. Those two tests are what keep the preview and the PATCH deliberately different.

## How this was produced

- One reviewer agent per area, nine in parallel.
- A validator and a refuter for each of the first 8 findings.
- REG-001's broader claim, that plainly malformed input also gets 422, came from its refuter. I checked it by reproducing NestJS's pipe code (zod 4.4.3, `@nestjs/core` from the main checkout's `node_modules`).

None of the findings or cleanups will be applied unless you ask. Say which ones to fix, ticket or skip.
